text: This is Painkiller: a platform that turns a conversation into running software, by orchestrating AI coding agents inside isolated Docker containers.
Building software means turning ideas into specs, specs into tasks, and tasks into code. Every handoff loses context. Painkiller automates the whole path, while keeping a human analyst in control.
It starts with an interview. A containerized agent runs the Superpowers brainstorming skill, asking the analyst one question at a time, often as clickable choices, until the idea is crystal clear.

The outcome is a written specification, versioned in the project's Git repository. That is spec-driven development: the spec is decomposed into small, atomic tasks, each with acceptance criteria and dependencies.

Each task is dispatched to its own sandboxed container, on its own feature branch. Painkiller is harness-agnostic: choose Antigravity with Gemini, or DeepSeek through dsh, Maki, or Unreal Agent. Every harness carries the same Superpowers skills: planning, test-driven development, and systematic debugging.
When an agent hits ambiguity, it does not guess. It asks, committing its work and exiting with code forty-two. The task pauses, the analyst answers, and the agent resumes right where it stopped.
When the agent finishes, the tests run in a fresh worker. Green means commit, merge, and complete. Every step streams live, and every token is counted against the project's budget.

Then comes deployment. Painkiller pushes to its built-in Gitea and hands the branch to Coolify. Each completed task can be tested on its own preview, and production is one click away. If a deploy fails, the log becomes a new task, and the agent fixes it.
Painkiller. From conversation, to spec, to production.
